notes: Experience is to be named 'Gaming Castle' - a title, not a build instruction.
P4 comes from space-staged plus teleporter-link read as portals to separate stages, which is what 'different mini games' means here.
The mini game stages are named as a segment with a null shape: the prompt says there are several and never says what any of them is, so the hole is recorded rather than filled with an invented shape.
The roulette table and friends are real geometry nobody plays. They are props inside a walkable build rather than a SET, so no SET flag is emitted.

notes_for_us: Emitting a segment with a null shape is the right answer for 'different mini games' and the rule for it is clear, but it means the biggest part of the build is a named hole. Worth knowing that a prompt can pass triage and still hand the pipeline almost nothing.

The non-playable machines are the interesting half of this prompt: real geometry, deliberately not interactive, inside a build the player walks around. SET is a whole-build flag, so there is no way to say 'this cluster is a set piece and the rest is walkable'. It ships as free text in image_prompt, which is probably fine, but the distinction the user made is lost.

notes_for_us: The Racing-versus-Vehicle-Sim boundary note settled this prompt in one line, and it needed settling: 'bikes, brands, ramps' reads as Racing until you notice nothing is being raced. Good rule, working as intended.

There is no option for a jump line or trick zone as such. physics-rig covers ramps as breakable physics props, which is not quite the same thing - a freestyle line is a sequenced series of takeoffs and landings with spacing that has to work, closer to Obby's path-track than to a ragdoll rig.

Third prompt in this batch where a preset's hazard-kill had to be flagged as contradicted. Across Action, Racing and Simulation it appears to be the default 'something dangerous' row and it lands on prompts with no lethal region at all.
